The challenge

Equipment problems don’t wait for office hours.

A pump trips. A temperature changes. An alarm appears among many others. The person who understands the equipment may be off site. Teams need a way to see what is happening and bring in the right expertise.

Remote access and security

Remote control shouldn’t mean exposed equipment.

Blinky-Lite uses publish-subscribe messaging, with devices initiating connections from inside the facility. Role-based permissions help control access to applications and data.

This is part of a layered approach. Security also depends on network protection, authentication, configuration and ongoing operation.

Learn about the architecture →

Open code. Expert integration.

Blinky-Lite is released under the MIT License. Customers retain access to the available code and can use and adapt it even if their support needs change.

BL Monitor and Control provides integration expertise. Customers can also use their own resources or engage another provider. Open source does not guarantee future maintenance, but it gives customers options.
